defect: AutoResearch control awaited an unowned native thread: cancellation released its async owner while writes continued. Scheduler/demotion/CLI management had no common root process owner, so a second caller could overwrite reports/runtime state. Sequential cycles shared clock-second identifiers and overwrote original cycle reports.8 controlled original cases establish these software mechanisms, not historical model/financial loss.
repair: Root-scoped process/thread ownership via the unchanged OS-held lock helper at a separate research-only path. Canonical absolute root is frozen before both work and guard, including CLI and standalone demotion, so a supported callback changing cwd cannot move writes outside the owned root. CLI owns before runtime writes and across daemon intervals; scheduler owns the full cycle, descendants may borrow only the actual thread service owner, nested cycles reject. Native control drains original worker on repeated cancellation; process-busy maps to rejected, not success/failed. UUID cycle identity plus existing-report rejection preserves old cycle reports.

ownership_contract.cli: Service lifetime acquired before runtime start/cycle/error/stop writes and held through daemon intervals or demotion-only. Busy CLI exits2 without changing the current owner artifacts.
ownership_contract.native_control: Owned worker completion, including repeated cancellation and errors, precedes async lock release. Cross-process busy is COMMAND_STATUS_REJECTED, not completed or an incorrectly failed research cycle.
ownership_contract.recovery: OS release after actual child death permits a new owner despite retained diagnostic marker. Marker age/TTL cannot take over a live owner. A root guard inode is never unlinked.
